problem: Prior VLN agents learn modality alignment from limited navigation data and generalize poorly to unseen scenes needing open-world knowledge (e.g. recognizing unseen landmarks). Directly plugging large models into embodied tasks brings noise because of the domain gap.
motivation: Landmark cooccurrence commonsense (fridge near stove) can substitute for hard-to-see mentioned landmarks. ChatGPT holds such priors but without visual grounding they can be inconsistent with the real scene and mislead the agent, so the priors must be corrected with actual observations.
key_idea: Cast VLN as open-world sequential landmark discovery: ChatGPT supplies ordered landmarks and cooccurrences, CLIP matches them to views, and a learnable scoring module re-weights cooccurrences per step; the corrected landmark features are added to observation features of existing VLN agents.
insight: Learnable scoring trained with a consistency loss on the ground-truth action suppresses noisy priors: LS adds about 0.8% SR/SPL over unscored priors across baselines (e.g. R2R-DUET SPL 60.64 to 61.51 to 63.02 with OE). Cooccurrences help (num=5 vs 0: +0.55 SR, +0.64 SPL) but 10 gives no more gain, and summation fusion works while concatenation is no better than the baseline. Stronger LLMs give better landmark extraction (Spacy worst, ChatGPT best SPL).
method: Landmark cooccurrence prior generation: few-shot ChatGPT prompts (5 examples for landmark extraction, 2 for cooccurrence) extract landmarks in navigational order and 5-10 visible cooccurrences per landmark, pre-extracted offline

Landmark shifting: a heuristic pointer z over adjacent landmarks; CLIP softmax between panorama-mean image feature and two landmark texts picks the current landmark; pointer forced to advance after 1-2 stuck steps
Landmark discovery: CLIP softmax over the candidate views for the current landmark and each of its cooccurrences (prompt 'a photo of a')

Learnable cooccurrence scoring: state feature from instruction [CLS] and view feature via linear+ReLU+LN+Dropout; dot-product with CLIP text feature gives scores that weight view probabilities, trained by cross-entropy consistency loss L_cs against the GT action

Observation enhancement: score-weighted sum of landmark text features per view is added to the agent's observation feature, with a symmetric contrastive loss L_ct between observation and corrected landmark features
Training: L = L_nav + 0.1 L_cs + 0.1 L_ct on top of HAMT or DUET, initialized from pretrained checkpoints; cooccurrences of R2R augmented data come from a nearest-landmark vocabulary

setting.backbone: HAMT / DUET (fine-tuned) + frozen CLIP ViT-B/32 + ChatGPT (offline prior generation)
setting.training_data: R2R/REVERIE/R4R/RxR-En training sets, plus R2R augmented data from HAMT; ChatGPT priors pre-extracted; agents initialized from pretrained baseline checkpoints
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (CLIP ViT-B/32 features) with directional info

numbers_note: R2R percent values are printed as integers in Table 1. The ablation table gives a more precise HAMT-based val-unseen result (SR 68.62, SPL 63.06), and DUET (SR 73.44, SPL 63.02). REVERIE main-table SPL for DUET+CONSOLE is 34.40, while the ablation table shows a different column arrangement.
results: CONSOLE consistently improves HAMT and DUET on R2R, REVERIE, R4R and RxR. On R2R DUET+CONSOLE reaches val-unseen SR 73 / SPL 63 (+3 SPL over DUET) and test-unseen SR 72 / SPL 61 (+2 SPL). It claims SOTA on R2R and R4R unseen excluding ScaleVLN, which uses far more data.
limitations: Relies on ChatGPT API for priors (cost; the R2R augmented data requires a vocabulary-matching approximation)
Landmark shifting is heuristic with a hand-set step threshold, and the CLIP features are frozen and pre-extracted
Gains are modest and it still trails ScaleVLN; evaluated only in discrete simulator settings
